I appreciate the perspective, but I'm going to stick with my actual view. I think there's a difference between being balanced and being wishy-washy.

Yes, there are some people who thrive in offices — those who struggle with self-direction, who need social connection at work, or who don't have good home environments. And some jobs genuinely require physical presence. I don't deny any of that.

But the research is pretty clear that for most knowledge workers, remote work is at least as productive and significantly better for well-being. And when you look at why many companies are pushing return-to-office mandates despite the evidence, control and status quo bias are major factors. It's not just about collaboration — it's often about managers feeling like they can't properly supervise people they can't see.

I can acknowledge nuances without pretending both sides are equally supported by the evidence.
